assumptions: OpenChemLib's torsion-library generator; the force field named; the `seed` fixes the draws.
limits: A sample of conformers, not an exhaustive search.
bio.jane/contract.question: What 3D conformers does this molecule take, and how is each scored?

description: 3D conformers of a small molecule by OpenChemLib's torsion-library generator, each scored and optionally minimized under MMFF94, MMFF94s or MMFF94s+ (whose MMFF94 equals Halgren's OPTIMOL on all 761 validation-suite structures), lowest energy first, as molfiles with every hydrogen; for a 3D molfile also the energy of its own geometry. Energies in kcal/mol.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

max_torsion_sets.description: distinct torsion sets to try before stopping.

molecule.description: the structure: SMILES or a molfile.

sixty_degree_steps.description: every rotatable bond in 60° steps instead of the torsion library's angles.

name: generate_conformers

conformers.description: each conformer: molfile, energy as generated and minimized (kcal/mol)

file_energy.description: a 3D molfile's own MMFF94 energy, or why it could not be computed

summary.description: the ensemble in words, generated from this run
